written: 2026-11-18, while the first SeedLM-2 model was training, before any SeedLM-2 result on held-out, validation or test tasks
candidates: every SeedLM-2 checkpoint trained by scripts/seedlm2_train.py; the one used downstream is the one with the most solved tasks on the extra pool's held-out fifth (best method), ties to the earlier checkpoint

methods.model: SeedLM-2's first beam proposal (width 32) that reproduces the visible example
methods.rerank: the engine's top-40 matches plus the model's verified proposals, ordered by the model's log-probability
methods.open: as rerank, with every operator in the model's beam treated as named so its keyword gate opens

choice: the method with the most solved held-out tasks (judged by each task's three asserts); ties go to rerank, then open, then model
gate: validation split, 1.5B branch-and-select pipeline with the chosen method in place of the engine: no fewer tasks solved than with the engine (31 of 45)
test: only after the gate: MBPP+ locked split once (1.5B and 0.5B stored pipelines) and HumanEval+ once, per reports/rule_pilot/humaneval_protocol.json

addendum_1.written: 2026-11-18, after the first checkpoint's held-out result (engine 65, model 49, rerank 60, open 60 of 94), before any validation or test use

added_methods.gate: the model only opens keyword gates (operators in its beam count as named); the engine still ranks
added_methods.tie: the model only breaks ties among the engine's best-scored programs
added_methods.fill: the model answers only where the engine has no program

addendum_1.why: rerank lost seven engine-correct answers for two gains: the model is less reliable than the engine's ranking where the engine is confident, so the new methods let it act only where the engine is weak
addendum_1.caveat: these three were added after looking at the held-out result, so the held-out choice among them is not clean; the validation gate and the single test and HumanEval+ runs are unchanged
